# Māratajjanīya Sutta (MN 50 (PTS MN i 332))

**ID:** MN 50 (PTS MN i 332)  
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Māratajjanīya Sutta  
**PTS:** MN i 332  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul4.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul4.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Multiple cross-language parallels exist: three Chinese versions are preserved, including a sutra in the *Madhyama-āgama* (MĀ 131, T 26) and two independent translations, the *Mo raoluan jing* (T 66) and the *Bimo shi mulian jing* (T 67, ca. 250 CE) [Bingenheimer]. A comparative detail noted between versions is that while the *Madhyama-āgama* parallel depicts laypeople spreading their hair on the ground out of respect instigated by Māra, MN 50 lacks this specific motif [Anālayo].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: MA 131 降魔; SHT Sutta 42; T 66 魔嬈亂; T 67 弊魔試目連
- Passage-level parallels: Thag 20.1 Mahāmoggallānattheragāthā
- Resembling parallels: SF 279 Māratajjanīya

**Sources**

- [Anālayo] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Mahāpajāpatī’s Going Forth in the Madhyama-āgama — Noted absence in MN 50 of laypeople spreading hair on the ground found in the Madhyama-āgama
- [Dayal 1932] Har Dayal, The Bodhisattva Doctrine in Buddhist Sanskrit Literature (1932) — Details of Moggallāna's former life as the Māra named Dūsī
- [Nyanaponika et al. 2003] Nyanaponika Thera, Hellmuth Hecker, and Bhikkhu Bodhi, Great Disciples of the Buddha (2003) — Context on Moggallāna's unique recollection of past lives in MN 50 and verse reuse with Thag 1187–1208
- [Appleton 2010] Naomi Appleton, Jātaka Stories in Theravāda Buddhism (2010) — Reference to Moggallāna's past birth under Buddha Kakusandha
- [Marino 2017] J. A. Marino, Metaphor and Pedagogy in Early Buddhist Literature (2017) — Citations of the alternate names for Mahāniraya described in MN 50 (MN i 337)
- [Polak 2011] Grzegorz Polak, Reexamining Jhāna (2011) — Account of Sañjīva entering cessation and surviving the funeral pyre under Buddha Kakusandha
- [Bingenheimer] Marcus Bingenheimer, Studies in Āgama Literature — Chinese parallels (MĀ 131, T 66, T 67) and narrative motif of Māra in Moggallāna's belly
